- AWS for a general-purpose, greenfield app. It has the broadest services, regions, ecosystem, and reliable managed building blocks (RDS/Aurora, ECS Fargate, Lambda, S3). Downsides: complexity and IAM learning curve.

Pick Azure if:
- You’re a Microsoft shop (AD, Windows/SQL Server, .NET, Office 365) and want strong licensing benefits (Azure Hybrid Benefit), tight identity integration, and enterprise support.
- You need hybrid/on‑prem integration (Azure Arc) or Windows-centric workloads.

Pick GCP if:
- Data/analytics/ML are first-class: BigQuery, Dataflow, Vertex AI, and generally the smoothest managed Kubernetes (GKE).
- You value clean networking/IAM models and developer ergonomics.
- You might use TPUs or want strong MLOps tooling.

Also consider:
- Cloudflare (edge workers, global latency-sensitive apps), Vercel/Netlify (front-end/serverless), Fly.io/Render (simple app hosting), DigitalOcean/Hetzner (cheap VMs, fewer managed services), OCI (aggressive pricing/egress, good for Oracle workloads).
- For Kubernetes-first teams: GKE is easiest; EKS/Aks are fine but require more tuning.
- For AI training: GCP (TPUs, A3 H100), Azure (NDv5 H100, strong OpenAI integration), AWS (P5/H100, Bedrock). Availability and quotas can be the tiebreaker.

runs.u: Which mobile carrier would you pick?
runs.reply:
I can pick a great one if I know a bit more. Quick questions:
- Where are you located (country + ZIP/postcode)?
- Top priority: best coverage, lowest price, or fastest data?
- How many lines?
- Do you travel internationally often? Any must-haves like hotspot or smartwatch support?

If you want a fast default (USA):
- Urban/suburban, best overall value: T-Mobile (Go5G/Essentials tiers). Great speeds, perks, and easy international roaming.
- Rural or max coverage: Verizon postpaid. Cheaper on the same network: Visible (great single-line value) or US Mobile (customizable, strong hotspot options).
- Balanced AT&T coverage: AT&T postpaid. Cheaper on the same network: Cricket.
- Frequent international travel: T-Mobile or Google Fi.
- Cheapest solid prepaid: Mint Mobile (T‑Mobile network) if coverage is good where you live.

Notes:
- MVNOs (Mint, Visible, US Mobile, Cricket) are cheaper but can be deprioritized during congestion.
- Check hotspot needs and eSIM support for your phone.

Share your location and priorities, and I’ll name the exact carrier and plan.
